born.why: The code prioritizes survival by strictly avoiding fruits with a history of harm unless proven safe, and only tastes novel fruits when hunger is moderate to avoid starvation risks, while eating known-safe fruits aggressively when hungry.

The code prioritizes survival by avoiding known poisons, eating proven safe foods when possible, and cautiously tasting novel foods to expand the safe diet list only when hunger levels justify the risk of a bad bite.

The code prioritizes survival by strictly avoiding known poisons, eating immediately when starving and the fruit is known safe, and carrying rather than eating if satiated to preserve resources, while cautiously tasting novel fruits only when hunger is moderate to minimize starvation risk during exploration.

It distinguishes between known-safe species (eats immediately), known-poisonous species (avoids unless starving), and uncertain ones (tastes for safety verification), using a majority vote on harm history to adapt to changing chemistry.

The code prioritizes avoiding known poisons (any harm history leads to leave/avoid), leverages positive history to eat fully without redundant tasting, and only tastes novel fruits when hunger is manageable to safely build a database of edible species.

It explicitly tracks safety status per species, avoids novel fruits with traits previously linked to harm (green/round), and prioritizes eating proven foods only when sufficiently hungry to avoid unnecessary foraging costs.

The code prioritizes survival by rejecting known poisons (where harms >= safes), exploiting safe foods immediately, and cautiously testing novel foods only when hunger is manageable, thus balancing exploration with starvation risk.
